gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Gamakay Phoenix V3 silent switch's "45 gf" is its force at 2.0 mm (35 gf initial, 58 gf at the bottom, 3.5 mm travel), which puts it next to Wooting's L60 (40/60 gf, 4.0 mm) and not the L45, or that the "0.125 ms" and "0.06 ms" latency claims on these boards are the 8 kHz report interval or less, against 0.60 ms that HLPlanet measured on Gamakay's sibling TK75 TMR.
standout_why: Compared against the pages I could read: the cited hlplanet.com guide, plus thegadgetverse.com and mechvibes.com from the result list. The HLPlanet guide names Phoenix V3 as essentially the only mainstream silent magnetic switch but gives no force, travel or dB for it and no rapid-trigger floor for a silent board. thegadgetverse lists Phoenix V3 force and travel as unpublished and says no lab has published a numeric noise score for a dedicated silent HE switch. Mechvibes has no dB figures and none of the three carded boards. None of them puts the makers' force labels, travel and latency claims on one basis. Two cited pages went unread: the RTINGS quiet-keyboards page served only navigation to my fetch, and the Reddit threads were blocked. So I could not rule out RTINGS holding a dBA figure for the NuPhy Air75 HE; that is why this is 2 and not 3.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's pick, the Gamakay TK75HE V2 with Phoenix V3 switches, and changes the reason. Nobody in the results publishes a dB figure, so silence has to be judged on switch construction, and Phoenix V3 is the only dedicated silent magnetic switch among the boards shown. The table adds two costs of that pick: 0.5 mm less travel than a Wooting Lekker (3.5 vs 4.0 mm) and a bottom-out as heavy as Wooting's L60. It also removes speed as a tiebreaker: the Epomaker HE68 Lite and Wooting 80HE both print 0.125 ms, which is just 1/8000 s, and Gamakay's 0.06 ms is under one 8 kHz interval. Fine-step claims (0.005 mm, 0.01 mm) are setting resolution; HLPlanet found release settings below about 0.3 mm misread on the sibling TK75 TMR. A shopper who already owns a Wooting 60HE can get the same silence for $13.99 in switches instead of a new board.

findings.product: Gamakay Phoenix V3 silent magnetic switch
findings.label: Force and travel, as HLPlanet's spec table lists them
findings.value: 35 gf minimum initial force, 45 ± 5 gf at 2.0 mm, 58 gf maximum end force, 3.50 ± 0.2 mm total travel
findings.source_title: Review: Gamakay Phoenix V3 Silent Magnetic Switch (HLPlanet, 2026-07-01)
findings.note: The headline "45 gf" is a mid-travel figure, not actuation or bottom-out. The same table lists initial flux 95 ± 15 Gs and bottom flux 580 ± 50 Gs. Mercury V3 (non-silent) is 30 gf initial, 55 gf end, same 3.50 mm travel.

findings.label: Lekker switch force and travel, for comparison
findings.value: Lekker L60: 40 gf actuation, 60 gf bottom-out, 4.0 mm total travel; Lekker L45: 30 gf actuation, 45 gf bottom-out, 4.0 mm
findings.source_title: Best Keyboards w/ Hall Effect magnetic switches [2026 GUIDE] (HLPlanet)
findings.note: Wooting names its switches by bottom-out force; Gamakay quotes force at 2.0 mm. On a like-for-like basis Phoenix V3 (35 to 58 gf) sits beside the L60 (40 to 60 gf), and has 0.5 mm less travel (4.0 − 3.5). Wooting's own page says the 80HE ships with Lekker L60 V2; HLPlanet's table does not say V1 or V2.

findings.label: Maker's US store price and headline claims
findings.value: $89.99 (list $119.99), in stock; "Ultra-low latency (0.06ms) meets 8 KHz polling"; title claims "0.005mm RT Accuracy"
findings.source_title: Gamakay TK75HE V2 Hall Effect keyboard 8K Polling Rate 0.005mm RT Accuracy
findings.note: Read through the store's search listing with storecheck.py; the product page itself returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so the per-switch variant price is not checked. Arithmetic: one 8 kHz report interval is 1/8000 s = 0.125 ms, so 0.06 ms is less than one interval and cannot be a key-press-to-PC figure.

findings.label: Measured latency and usable rapid-trigger floor on the sibling board with the same Phoenix V3 switches
findings.value: HLPlanet measured 0.60 ms wired and 0.75 ms on 2.4 GHz with OSLTT; release settings below about 0.3 mm can misread from plate flex, about 0.4 mm suggested
findings.note: This is the TK75 TMR, not the TK75HE V2. The spec table there lists 8,000 Hz wired and 2.4 GHz, 1,000 Hz Bluetooth, "0.01 mm precision" rapid trigger, 0.01 to 3.0 mm actuation, 8,000 mAh, $119.99. The measured 0.60 ms is 10 times the 0.06 ms Gamakay prints for the TK75HE V2 (0.60 / 0.06). No measured latency for the TK75HE V2 itself was read.
